_about: OUR editorial topic tags for measures, so readers can find what they care about. Each tag needs a one-line factual `why` grounded in the official digest or analysis. Tags say what a vote DOES, not whether it's good. `on` is the vote that causes the effect ("yes", the default, or "no"). `effect` is "up" (raises, funds or expands), "down" (cuts or limits), "stable" (keeps an existing tax at today's level, e.g. making a temporary tax permanent), "limit" (restricts FUTURE taxes, changes no current tax) or omitted. Tax tags add `share` (roughly how many are affected) and `affects_if` (short, single-filer terms). Schema: docs/data-model.md.

topics.label: Ethics & corruption
topics.description: Oversight of officials, contracting integrity, campaign money.

topics.label: Bureaucracy reform
topics.description: How government is organized, staffed, audited or permits things.

topics.label: Business taxes
topics.description: Taxes paid by businesses and commercial property. Each tag sits on the vote that causes it: ↑ raises, ↓ cuts or limits, = keeps today's rate (e.g. making a temporary tax permanent), ⊘ limits future taxes.

topics.label: Personal taxes
topics.description: Taxes paid by individuals and households. Each tag sits on the vote that causes it: ↑ raises, ↓ cuts or limits, = keeps today's rate (e.g. making a temporary tax permanent), ⊘ limits future taxes.

topics.label: Regressive tax
topics.description: A tax that takes a larger share of income from lower-income households, such as a sales tax.

topics.label: Progressive tax
topics.description: A tax aimed at high earners or the very wealthy.

topics.label: Housing construction
topics.description: Funds, finances or speeds up building homes.

topics.label: Elections & democracy
topics.description: How measures, recalls and votes work.

prop-1.why: $11.25B in state bonds for affordable housing programs, including multifamily rentals and supportive housing.

prop-3.affects_if: you're a single filer earning over ~$371K
prop-3.why: Makes permanent the 2012 rates on income over about $371K (single filers; $742K joint, $505K head of household). Without it they expire in 2031.
Applies only to the top ~2% of California taxpayers by income.

prop-3.affects_if: you're a single filer earning over ~$371K (from 2031)
prop-3.why: A NO vote lets the higher rates expire in 2031 for income over about $371K (single filers; $742K joint, $505K head of household), using 2025 thresholds adjusted for inflation.

prop-4.why: Lets state and local governments create public financing programs for candidates' campaigns.
Changes how campaigns can be funded.

prop-5.why: Removes the replacement-candidate question from statewide recall elections.

prop-37.why: Creates a state loan program for middle-income buyers of newly built homes, funded by up to $25B in revenue bonds.

prop-40.affects_if: your net worth was over $1 billion on Jan 1, 2026
prop-40.why: One-time tax of 5% of net worth on billionaires who lived in California on Jan 1, 2026. The LAO says California has “a few hundred” of them.

prop-41.why: Bars new state taxes whose revenue is excluded from the state spending limit.
Bars new state taxes whose revenue is excluded from the state spending limit.
Requires State Auditor reviews of programs funded by special taxes.

prop-42.why: Prohibits new state taxes on owning financial assets or other personal property, and certain retroactive taxes.
Prohibits new state taxes on owning financial assets or other personal property, and certain retroactive taxes.

prop-43.why: Requires two-thirds voter approval for certain local taxes that can now pass by majority.
Requires two-thirds voter approval for certain local taxes that can now pass by majority.

prop-45.why: Tightens environmental-review timelines and narrows court challenges for housing and other projects.

rtm.why: Funds BART, Muni, Caltrain and other operators for 14 years (~$980M/yr regionwide).
A sales tax takes a larger share of income from lower-income households.

rtm.affects_if: you buy taxable goods in SF (1% sales tax)
rtm.why: Adds a 1% sales tax in San Francisco for 14 years.

prop-a.why: Eliminates, merges or moves dozens of commissions and advisory bodies out of the Charter.

prop-b.why: Authorizes a city finance corporation (and later a public bank) whose lending includes affordable housing. It doesn't fund one.

prop-c.why: Raises the City's yearly Housing Trust Fund contribution toward $125M and extends the fund to 2058.

prop-d.why: Raises signature requirements for initiatives (2% to 8%) and ends ballot placement by the Mayor or four Supervisors.

prop-e.why: Centralizes purchasing rules under the City Administrator.
Raises the contract size needing Board approval from $10M to $25M.

prop-f.why: Expands the Mayor's power to reorganize departments and hire and fire department heads.

prop-h.why: Funds Muni service with ~$177M/yr for 15 years.

prop-h.share: ~39% of SF households own their home
prop-h.affects_if: you own SF property ($129+/yr; most owners 65+ pay less or nothing)
prop-h.why: New annual parcel tax for 15 years. Owners of rent-controlled units can pass up to 50%, capped at $65 per unit per year, to tenants whose rent was set before June 1, 2027.

prop-h.affects_if: you own commercial property in SF ($799+/yr, capped at $400K)
prop-h.why: New annual parcel tax on non-residential and mixed-use property.

prop-i.why: Dedicates half of transfer-tax revenue from $10M+ property sales to affordable housing and housing assistance.

prop-j.affects_if: a lender takes commercial or large residential property in foreclosure
prop-j.why: Applies the 0.5%–6% transfer tax to foreclosure transfers of commercial, industrial and large residential properties. Smaller residential buildings keep the exemption.
